reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that mechanical alloying and SPS can produce oxide precipitates (TiO) that strengthen a refractory HEA, but it does not address Y2O3 additions, high-temperature (1273 K) mechanical behavior, or the specific TiVNbTa system. The key premises about Y2O3 dispersion, high-temperature strengthening mechanisms, and predicted strength improvement lack direct prior support.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a refractory HEA via mechanical alloying and SPS
Nano-oxide dispersions inhibit dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding at high temperature
Such dispersions suppress recovery, grain coarsening, and thermal softening
This mechanism will significantly improve yield strength at 1273 K over the baseline TiVNbTa alloy
